 Print 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion', featuring Ajay Devgn and Tabu , continues to maintain its impressive box office record despite entering its seventh week in theatres. The crime thriller collected Rs 12 lakh net in India on Day 43, taking its domestic net earnings to Rs 380.31 cr. Its worldwide gross collection has now reached Rs 588.55 cr, including contributions from overseas markets. According to Sacnilk, the movie has secured a blockbuster verdict. The film's latest figures, updated until November 13, indicate a 14.3% decline in daily collections compared to the previous day. It recorded 75 shows across the country on Friday. Although its daily earnings have slowed, the movie continues to maintain a substantial cumulative total. Its India gross collection currently stands at Rs 455.35 cr, while international markets have contributed Rs 133.20 cr.  The Ajay Devgn starrer earned Rs 12 lakh net and Rs 14 lakh gross in India on its 43rd day. The film is currently running in its seventh week, with its latest performance indicating the expected slowdown during an extended theatrical run. Its domestic net earnings have reached Rs 380.31 cr, while the India gross total stands at Rs 455.35 cr. The worldwide gross collection has climbed to Rs 588.55 cr. Overseas territories account for 22.6% of the global earnings, with the Indian market contributing the remaining 77.4%. Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar 
 Ajay Devgn reprises his role as Vijay Salgaonkar in the latest instalment of the 'Drishyam' franchise. Tabu returns as Meera Deshmukh, while Shriya Saran, Ishita Dutta and Mrunal Jadhav are also part of the cast. The ensemble further features Rajat Kapoor, Prakash Raj and Jaideep Ahlawat. The narrative follows Vijay Salgaonkar as he faces another challenge years after successfully evading the law. His efforts to keep his family protected encounter fresh obstacles when the investigation gains renewed momentum. Meera Deshmukh also returns, but her intentions have shifted from seeking justice to pursuing revenge. Jaideep Ahlawat's face-off with Ajay Devgn
 The confrontation between Ajay Devgn and Jaideep Ahlawat is among the notable elements highlighted in the ETimes review. The publication awarded the film 3.5 stars out of 5, praising the emotional depth brought by the lead actor's performance. The review read, "Ultimately, it is Ajay Devgn who gives Drishyam its emotional edge. There is an inherent niceness to his screen presence that makes Vijay easy to empathise with, even when you question his choices. His decision to bury a crime is hardly morally defensible, but Devgn makes you understand why this man believes he is doing what he has to do. Join conversation
